transcript.text: theres water in the bottom of my frige under the salad draws, keeps comming back after i mop it up

Water pooling under the salad drawers in a fridge-freezer is almost always caused by a blocked defrost drain. When the fridge cycles off, frost melts and runs down the back wall into a small drain hole; if that hole gets clogged with food or gunk, the water has nowhere to go and backs up onto the shelves. To check this safely: please unplug the appliance first. Look at the bottom of the rear interior wall for a small drain hole or channel. Is it visible, and does it look blocked by debris or ice?

ok i found it, theres a little groove and a hole at the bottom of the back wall and its got bits of lettuce and gunk in it. water is only inside the fridge not near the plug btw. what do i do to clear it?

[Heading: Blocked defrost drain]
That confirms it is a blocked defrost drain; the lettuce and gunk are stopping the meltwater from escaping, which is why it keeps pooling. To clear it safely, please unplug the fridge first. Use a turkey baster or syringe with warm (not boiling) water to gently flush the hole and groove until the debris clears and water runs freely into the back of the appliance. If there is stubborn gunk, you can carefully use a flexible pipe cleaner or a piece of soft wire to dislodge it, but avoid forcing anything that could puncture the internal lining. Once clear, pour another small amount of warm water to confirm it drains away quickly.
ok thanks, i dont have a turkey baster but i have cotton buds, would that do for the gunk then warm water after? ill try it now

[Heading: Blocked defrost drain cleared]
Cotton buds are actually perfect for this because they let you reach into the small hole without pushing debris further in. Once the visible blockage is gone, slowly pour a little more warm water into the groove to check that it flows away freely down the drain. If you can hear or see the water disappearing into the back of the fridge, you have successfully fixed the issue.
ok did it, got the gunk out with the cotton bud and poured warm water in and it went straight down the hole. no more puddle over the next few days either, so looks sorted. thanks!

[Heading: Blocked defrost drain cleared]
That is excellent news. Since the water drained away immediately and hasn't returned in a few days, you have successfully resolved the issue by clearing the blockage. The pooling was definitely caused by that debris stopping the defrost water from escaping. To help prevent this happening again, try to keep food items slightly forward of the rear wall so they don't trap moisture against it, and check the drain hole occasionally if you notice any condensation building up inside.
